reader.requirement: At --std 85 every nonnumeric literal (the only quoted literal form 1985 has: quotation-mark delimited, no X/N/B prefix, no apostrophe) is of category alphanumeric, so it moves as an alphanumeric sender (to numeric as an unsigned integer, §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4 b 3), compares as a nonnumeric operand against a numeric integer item (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2), and is refused wherever a numeric literal is required (arithmetic operands, PERFORM TIMES integer, VALUE of a numeric item).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry gates on the literal forms later editions added (national N"", boolean B"", hexadecimal X"", zero-length, apostrophe delimiter): refused at 85 with COBOL0900, admitted at 2023; a plain quotation-mark literal passes no gate at either edition
the literal's length rule per edition

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the category itself (BoundStringLiteral defaults to Alphanumeric at every edition); the set of literal forms that are alphanumeric differs (85 has only the quotation-mark form; X"" and apostrophes are 2002 introductions, refused at 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises only the nonnumeric comparison against a numeric integer item; MOVE of a nonnumeric literal to numeric, numeric-edited, alphabetic, alphanumeric-edited and group receivers and the refusals in numeric-only positions are not exercised

probes.expected: alphanumeric sender: "123" to 99V9 moves as integer 123 -> 23.0; "12" to 9(4) -> 0012; to alphabetic/alnum-edited/group legal; N3=5 vs "005" equal, vs "5" (space-extended) not equal

probes.printed: error COBOL0844: an alphanumeric literal is not a numeric operand
error COBOL5506: The alphanumeric literal "2" is not expected here: only an integer literal
error COBOL1657: the VALUE literal "12" is alphanumeric but the item is numeric
error COBOL2532: a numeric operand compared with an operand of class alphanumeric shall be an integer
error COBOL3318: a class condition's subject shall be identifier-1, not a literal
error COBOL0900: the hexadecimal alphanumeric literal X"..." requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)

reader.notes: One mapping (ExpressionBinder.NonNumericLiteralOperand) binds every quoted literal to BoundStringLiteral, whose Category defaults to Alphanumeric; the 1985 edition differs only in which literal forms exist, gated position-blind by LiteralScreen.GateFormat. Classes a, e, f do not bear on a literal's category. The refusal diagnostics cite §2023 clauses, a wording matter only.

refuter.evidence: Attack on the 1985-only comparison restriction the reader did not probe ('Numeric and nonnumeric operands may be compared only when their usage is the same'): src/nl_comp.cob IF C2 = "12" with C2 PIC 99 COMP -> error COBOL2532 at 85 (and at 2023), refused as 1985 requires. src/nl_misc.cob at 85: S99 VALUE -12 = "12" EQ, SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -12 = "12" EQ, "12" = group EQ, 12 < "2" LT (alphanumeric compare, space-extended), doubled quote A"B, "1.5" moved as alphanumeric, "AB1" to PIC A legal, continued literal. Class c: src/nl_apos.cob 'AB' -> COBOL0900 (2002 form); src/nl_empty.cob "" -> COBOL0900 (2014 form); src/nl_concat.cob "AB" & "CD" -> COBOL0900 (2002). cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.3 GR3 'All nonnumeric literals are of category alphanumeric'; OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 (lies in its usage paragraph) 'Numeric and nonnumeric operands may be compared only when their usage is the same'. The 160-character minimum length is an implementor floor, not a ceiling, so no refusal is required above it.
